notes: Ground truth + full validation matrix for the purpose-built UAT storefront fixture (12 Python source files, one framework = Flask, one manifest = requirements.txt). This file EXTENDS the corpus convention (`source` + `findings` + `expected_unresolved`, keyed by file/severity/source with citation-substring anchors; line numbers are approximate anchors, not exact-match assertions) with three added blocks the richer UAT expectation needs: `expected_killed` (falsify should kill these), `expected_map` (map/ architecture + production-exposure ground truth), and `planted_cases` (the per-case matrix required by the UAT spec). The two scripted-golden fixtures are NOT touched; this fixture is a Tier-2 benchmark-corpus fixture (has an `expected_findings.json`, is not in conftest.FIXTURE_LLM), so it is scored by the live model / real tools, never by canned answers.

field_provenance.note: Field names in `planted_cases[].exposure` mirror the current (risk-quant session B) output shapes so they are directly validatable — confirmed against store/models.py and analyze/ this session, not the session-A shape.
field_provenance.exposure_component_range: store.models.DealRisk.exposure_component in [0,1]; the same value flows into RiskScenario.exposure_factors[] (analyze/risk_quant.build_scenarios derived_exposures).
field_provenance.control_strength_expected: RiskScenario.control_strengths[] — 0.0 conservative default for confirmed findings (no structured positive-control evidence); killed candidates never reach risk_quant.
field_provenance.expected_disposition: store.models.FalsificationStatus — confirmed|killed|unresolved(=requires-review). `architecture-exposure` is used for case 6, which is a map/exposure expectation, not a falsification verdict.

source.framework_rationale: Flask maximizes coverage of the pipeline's own tooling: requirements.txt is the SCA adapter's native manifest, Python has first-class AST support in detect/retrieval, gitleaks/semgrep/pip-audit are all first-class on this stack, and @app.route entry points are what the map stage recovers cleanly. See README.md.
source.not_derived_from: Authored from scratch for this fixture. NOT adapted from OWASP Juice Shop or any existing project; the vulnerability set is a controlled 10-case test matrix.
source.safety: Intentionally insecure and inert by default — see snapshot/SECURITY.md. wsgi.py refuses to self-serve without STOREFRONT_ALLOW_RUN=1 and then binds 127.0.0.1 only with the debugger off. The pipeline only ever reads these files statically; it never imports or runs the app.

fake_credential.note: Recognizable placeholder, not a working secret. Confirmed gitleaks-detectable this session (rule `stripe-access-token`, the only leak it reports).

advisories.summary: Requests before 2.20.0 sends the HTTP Authorization header to an http URI upon a same-hostname https->http redirect, leaking credentials to a network sniffer.

source.advisory_notes: requests==2.19.1 is genuinely old, so real SCA tools will additionally surface other real, OSV-verified requests advisories (e.g. CVE-2023-32681, CVE-2024-35195). Those are acceptable extra hits, not fabricated; the DESIGNATED, stable case-5 CVE is CVE-2018-18074. Flask 3.0.3 is pinned for a runnable app; the fixture does not attempt to track a moving CVE-clean Flask/Werkzeug baseline (see README 'flagged dependency gaps').

findings.title: SQL injection in public product search
Server-side request forgery in admin link-preview
IDOR: order readable without an ownership check

expected_unresolved.reason: Reflected/stored `next` value with no server-side redirect sink in-repo; exploitability depends on out-of-scope frontend consumption. Single source (no corroboration) and falsify cannot confidently confirm or kill -> unresolved -> review.

expected_killed.reason: Structurally identical to the IDOR (case 3) but guarded by the @owns_resource("invoice") ownership gate (defined in storefront/security.py). falsify/'s mitigating-control retrieval should surface the decorator and KILL the candidate -> a correctly-killed candidate, not a surviving false positive.

Real OS-command-injection pattern in dead code: legacy_bp is never registered by the app factory (storefront/__init__.py) AND the handler is gated behind ENABLE_LEGACY_IMPORT which is permanently False. falsify/'s reachability check should KILL it as unreachable.

expected_map.note: Architecture the map/ stage should recover. Validates case 6 (production-like customer datastore) and supplies the trust-boundary/entity FKs that findings anchor to and that deal_risk.py's production-exposure check reads.

data_stores.why: System of record for customer personal data; orders/invoices FK to it. This is the case-6 production-like store deal_risk.py should score as direct exposure.

planted_cases.disposition_basis: falsify confirms attacker-controlled query param woven into SQL, reachable from the public edge, no mitigating control.
planted_cases.notes: Query runs against the customer datastore; a UNION reaches customer PII, reinforcing the case-6 exposure.

planted_cases.disposition_basis: admin-gated but the fetched URL is fully caller-controlled and fetched server-side from inside the deployment network (can reach internal/metadata endpoints).
planted_cases.notes: This is the 'command-injection OR SSRF -> SSRF' choice. The `requests` client here is also the case-5 vulnerable dependency (distinct finding: code CWE-918 vs dependency CWE-522).

planted_cases.disposition_basis: Authenticates the caller but never checks the order's customer_id against the session; any signed-in customer reads any order. Query is parameterized (not SQLi).
planted_cases.notes: This is the 'broken authorization OR IDOR -> IDOR' choice. Single-source (semgrep is weak on IDOR); its severity upgrade is licensed by a falsify-confirmed reachability pass, not by corroboration. Pairs with case 7 (the defended twin).

planted_cases.disposition_basis: Live-pattern (sk_live_) credential committed in source; gitleaks-detectable, obviously-fake value.
planted_cases.notes: Also serves as case 10: flagged by BOTH gitleaks (source_tool=secrets, confirmed this session) and the owasp LLM lens on the same line -> matching.py line-overlap merge -> db.list_countable_findings collapses to ONE countable finding, not two.

planted_cases.disposition_basis: requests==2.19.1 is < 2.20.0; SCA (pip-audit / OSV) flags CVE-2018-18074. Real, OSV-verified.
planted_cases.notes: SCA adapter emits severity=medium and anchors to manifest line 1 (whole-manifest convention). Designated CVE is CVE-2018-18074; other real requests advisories may also fire (acceptable, all OSV-verified).

planted_cases.disposition_basis: Not a falsification verdict: the map/ stage should recover a `customers` DataStore holding PII (email/full_name/shipping_address/card_last4) behind the production-like storefront edge, so deal_risk.py's production-exposure check resolves findings that touch it to production_exposure=direct with a high exposure_component. Validated via `expected_map.data_stores` + the exposure blocks of cases 1 and 3, and the RiskScenario.exposure_factors they feed.
planted_cases.trust_boundary: public storefront edge -> authenticated customer session
planted_cases.notes: The customer datastore is what makes the fixture's trust boundary genuinely production-like; without it deal_risk.py's production-exposure check would have nothing real to resolve.

planted_cases.disposition_basis: Looks like the case-3 IDOR (by-id resource fetch), but the route is decorated @owns_resource("invoice"), which enforces invoice.customer_id == current_customer_id() (defined in storefront/security.py). falsify/'s mitigating-control retrieval should surface the decorator and KILL the candidate.
planted_cases.notes: Success criterion: this candidate is CORRECTLY KILLED by the mitigating-control search, not surviving as a false positive and not silently dropped (its killed verdict + reason persist in the store).

planted_cases.disposition_basis: Real os.system() command-injection pattern, but doubly dead: legacy_bp is never registered by the app factory, and the handler is gated behind ENABLE_LEGACY_IMPORT which is permanently False. falsify/'s reachability check should KILL it as unreachable.
planted_cases.notes: Success criterion: falsify identifies unreachability and kills it. If a scanner flags the os.system sink, the kill (not a survive) is the correct outcome.

planted_cases.disposition_basis: A `next` value is stored on the session and echoed back, but the backend never redirects to it — there is no server-side redirect sink in-repo. Exploitability (open redirect) depends on out-of-scope frontend behavior, so falsify can neither confirm nor kill, and it is uncorroborated (single lens). Reliability layer -> unresolved -> review/ per the licensing rule.
planted_cases.notes: Success criterion: routed to review/ as unresolved (a ReviewRequest opens), NOT silently confirmed or killed. It must lack both corroboration and a confident falsification verdict for this to hold.

planted_cases.disposition_basis: Same physical finding as case 4. gitleaks (source_tool=secrets) and the owasp LLM lens both flag the sk_live_ key on the same line; matching.py matches on line-overlap and db.list_countable_findings collapses the group to a single countable finding.
planted_cases.notes: Rides on case 4 (per the UAT spec: 'a single real issue ... written so two independent sources both flag it'). Success criterion: exactly ONE countable finding after matching, corroborated_by shows the second source; two sources must NOT double-count.
